We decided to buy the other jug when we found the Rubbermaid on sale at a local store for less than 1/3rd the cost of the more sturdy jug. For the difference in price we thought we'd give the Rubbermaid a try to see how it would perform.

The lower spigot on the Rubbermaid is solid. No leaks and easy to use. The upper vent spigot is a little bit of a weak point. It works absolutely fine, just remember to always close it so it doesn't get broken or let hot air cycle into the cold interior of the jug.

Although not an "extreme" cooler jug, once filled with ice and water we had cold water well into the second day in the desert. The cooler was kept in the shade the entire time.

If you need a rough and tumble water jug, look elsewhere. If you need something that will sit on a picnic table for a day or two, this will work fine.

It can be clipped onto clothing and such with a metal clip that's on the back. I use this when I'm out walking for exercise. Or the provided pieces allow you to loop a rubber grip around a tube (handle, bike seatpost, etc.) and attach it to a plastic piece that the light will clip into. The metal clip has a square cut-out that snaps over a plastic button/projection in the bike grip to hold it securely in place. You lift the clip off this button and slide the clip up and off when you need to charge it.

The bottom of the light is removable and you plug the light directly into a USB charging port to charge the light. The bottom (USB connector cover) is easy to remove without being in any danger of falling off by itself. The power button is on top and pressing it cycles between modes: all lights on high, on medium, on low, slow blinking, warning flashes, and fast blinking. Press the power button for 2 seconds to turn off. It's bright, small, and easy to use for my purposes--warning people I'm there and to watch out for me. Power: 1 W. Charge current: 0.5A. Battery: lithium. Net weight: 4g.

In the video, the first three modes look about the same because the camera compensates for the lower light level, but it is getting progressively dimmer.

text_fidelity_a:
Razor 13113614 E300 Electric Scooter Love it! Using it for short errands in the neighborhood. Unfortunately it seems that there is no way to moderate speed. Its either off or full on.

UPDATE: Downgraded from 5 to 4 stars.
It CRITICAL that your rear tire is fully inflated to the recommended pressure. Your new scooter may come with under-inflated tires and it needs HUGE WARNING IN RED LETTERS to inform people to inflate rear tire.

If the rear tire is under inflated,, when torque is applied to the rear wheel, it might start to slip inside the tire. This will eventually cause a damage to the air valve letting more air out. That will in turn result in more slippage until the valve gets completely sheared off of the inner tube, cause ALL air to rapidly escape. You might lose control of the scooter, or, if you don't, you will have to push it all the way back home.

TYR SPORT EBP Burner Fin (Color of Fin is By Size) Anyone who swims competitively or simply to stay in shape should get a pair of these! I used them several years ago while on a swim team and forgot how good they are, so I bought another pair recently. A few things about these fins:

TYR's sizing chart worked great for me. I wear 10.5 shoes, so I bought size large for shoe sizes 9-11. This worked perfect for me. They slip on easy, and they seemed to stay on fine. Once they were on I never had to adjust them. I would recommend putting them on once in the water. They are also quite easy to walk in, and I had no problem at all doing flip turns with them.

These fins are definitely geared toward competitive swimmers because they have short blades. This allows you to kick at a faster cadence, unlike long blade fins that require minimal kicking. I would highly recommend buying these instead of long blade fins if you are a lap swimmer. They give you a great workout and really make your legs burn.

I have no issues with mine. The fit is perfect, the material is a strong rubber, the color on my large fins is a nice looking red and black. No issues with them hurting my feet or toes. It is possible to get blisters on the back of your ankles if you do not buy a correct size, and/or wear these for a long swim, so keep that in mind. Some people wear socks which helps if the fins are too big, but I would just follow their size chart and you will be fine.

Highly recommend for the price and what they do for your workout.
text_fidelity_b: TYR SPORT EBP Burner Fin (Color of Fin is By Size)

text_fidelity_a:
Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle I've had this bike a few months now. It is quiet (but not silent, there is a noise from the drive belt) but it is very smooth and responsive.

Assembly was straight-forward, but unless you want to find all the tools you need to assemble it yourself, I would recommend getting the tool package available on their website. The torque wrench was our deciding factor in just buying their kit. Keiser offers a discount on the tool package if you purchase it with the bike directly on their website.

Things to know: the app is TERRIBLE. Other reviewers have already listed all the bugs in depth, but the app is unreliable for recording workouts and is not user-friendly. The bike also will not work directly with other apps (like Peloton). For that you need the converter, which costs another $200 on top of this bike, unless you buy the bike directly from their website. Then it is only $50. Considering they were discounting it 75% with purchase of the bike, I consider $200 a rip-off for what your bike should have done in the first place (work with other apps). I wrote customer service about the bugs. They agreed there was a problem and the developer would be notified. I was told I would be updated when it was fixed. I never was. The problem in the app still persists as of my writing this review.

Customer service: I wrote customer service via email. As far as timeliness, they wrote back quickly. However, if I ever had more than one question in my message, one, and only one, of my questions would be answered. I had to write back multiple times for my additional questions to be answered, so one simple email took several days to be fully addressed. As stated above, some of the issues never were.

I will update the review if any issues with the bike itself come up. I love the bike, how smooth it runs, and the huge range of resistances available. It seems well-designed and like it will hold up. However, there are some big annoyances that will cost you extra $$$ to overcome.
text_fidelity_b: Keiser M3i Indoor Cycle Bundle

Texture is very crumbly, which is actually a good thing as it makes these rations easy to eat even for those with poor or no teeth.

Perfect, neutral and easy to eat is exactly how emergency rations should be. If you need to bust into these, there's no reason the rations should be terrible and make an already unpleasant situation worse by having to eat terrible food, too. At the same time, they're not good enough that anyone's going to be getting into them without a need. Not conducive to frivolous snacking. The outer package is easy to open, the inner plastic shrink wrap on the individual bars was surprisingly difficult to get open. Completely doable, but a knife or sharp pokey object will make it easier.

I also use it to massage the sides of my hips, again pinned up against the wall.

If you ever get tense muscles I would highly recommend trying one of these out! I received this product for free/at a discounted rate in exchange for my honest review. I'm very happy with the product and can confidently say it is a 5 star quality product.

text_fidelity_a: Wahoo TICKR Heart Rate Monitor, Bluetooth/ANT+ I bought this to replace a dying Garmin HRM I had.  Instantly, out of the box, you can tell the product design is better by the battery cover.  My garmin had 4 eye-glass screws that were easy to strip or gouge, while the Wahoo has a large sealed plastic cap (much less likely to break).  While cycling, I've almost never had any slippage or inaccurate readings, so I can't complain there.  While running though, the band's enclosure system is more difficult to synch tight and keep properly when you're running and sweating heavily.  It's a detriment of soft straps, but my old Garmin had pads that 'stuck' more to you.  All in all though, I'm super pleased; my work-around is just to make it really tight and then it'll loosen a bit as I run.  Data quality is very high (have compared to other HRM simultaneously)

When attempting to install the rack onto a 2" hitch, noticed that the bolt didn't screw in. Learned from reading many reviews of bike racks NEVER to force it in, so took it out. Read online that the threads in the receiver may have some bits and pieces of excess metal (due to hasty manufacturing) that was causing the bolt to get stuck. Found out that this can be easily fixed if you "clean up" the threads in the receiver using a 1/2" steel drill tap (and WD-40). Bought one for $5 and screwed in the tap just like you would the bolt. The drill tap took off the excess metal. Tried the bolt next, and screwed into the receiver hole nicely.

A similar situation happened with the top of the rack: the hole for the folding arms was too small for the bolt on one side, and needed to be widened. No problem. Spent another $5 to buy a round metal file, and filed inside the hole, widening it. Problem solved.

Now many customers don't want to take the time and money to fix these minor annoyances. They want the product to be perfect and easily installed. But the product is solid, and under normal circumstances would receive 5 Stars. Because of the extra work, must give it 3 Stars.
text_fidelity_b: Swagman TRAILHEAD 3 Fold Down Bike Rack

Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177) Back in 1977 I purchased one of the first models of this pistol, and used it for years. Around 2003 I lost it. Long story short I loaned it to someone and never got it back. Guessing you know the moral to that story.

Just recently I've gotten the urge to do some target shooting in my back yard - I can probably blame watching episodes of [[ASIN:B003NX6C1C Top Shot]] for that. So I wanted to replace my 1377, mainly because I still had all the accessories for it. So I got on Amazon and found this one to purchase.

To be honest, I did not read the information on the product page - just ordered it. A few days later I had the pistol in my hands. First thing I noticed is it's not quite the gun I remember having. Apparently the design has been changed. Gone was the pull knob that you used to cock the gun and instead there is a breach mechanism. I think I actually like the new design better.

One of the biggest surprise for me was that this model no longer makes use of Bbs. Gone is the magnetic tip on the end of loading pin. Wish I had know that before including this package in my order - [[ASIN:B000HKKY7M Crosman Copperhead 6000 Copper Coated BBs in a Bottle]]. But, that is my fault for not paying attention to what was on the product page.

Anyway - even just shooting pellets I am having fun with this gun. I also bought packs of these pellets - [[ASIN:B001DCB61Q Crosman Destroyer .177 Cal, 7.9 Grains, Pointed, 250ct]] & [[ASIN:B002DM0ZIU Crosman Hollow Point Pellets, 0.177-Calibre]]. Both seem to work well.

I've been having a lot of fun plinking cans and shooting targets. I think this pellet gun is great.
text_fidelity_b: Crosman American Classic Pump Air Pistol (.177)

text_fidelity_a:
HPDMC 110v 300bar Portable Air Compressor Paintball Fill Station for PCP Game This is really a nice compressor for filling pcp rifles. I did get it from a different seller at a much better price. Fill times for my wildfire pcp from 1000 to 2000 psi is about 35 seconds. For my Hatsan At44 tanks (180cc) from 2000 to 3000 psi is about 45 seconds. Unit stays under 125˚F. Couple of hints for optimal running. The water inlet is actually the lower inlet. Make sure to start the pump first. Start the compressor with the bleed valve open. DO NOT stop the compressor while under a load, open the bleed valve first. Leave the water pump running for a bit after shutting down the compressor. Make sure to remove and dry the filter in the fill line after every use. This has made my shooting so much more fun and easy.
Update: I have over 2 years on this compressor now. Zero issues. I added another inline moisture filter (about $40 here on amazon) and recently checked my gun cylinders (adding regulators) and there was NO moisture at all. I do frequent oil changes on this compressor with Royal Purple full synth. (every 50 to 75 fills or about 2 to 3 hours run time). I did add Cooper wire wraps around the SS tubes to help desperate heat more efficiently (and to help keep myself from burning my arm accidentally). I got this off flea-bay and went to purchase another one but the price has jumped a bit (249 to 349) Seller a toreal2018.
text_fidelity_b: HPDMC 110v 300bar Portable Air Compressor Paintball Fill Station for PCP Game

text_fidelity_a: TR Oversized Folding Directors Chairs with Side Table, Heavy Duty Portable Camping Chair for Adults Support 350-lb for Outdoor Picnic Lawn Hunting (Brown) [[VIDEOID:38f3fac988bc186a50d2347de335d1eb]] I’d sat on a similar chair when we visited my sister-in-law and her family camping last summer and I was thinking we needed to get one or two for ourselves. When I had the chance to grab this TR Lightweight Directors Chairs with Side Table I took it and we are so glad I did! It arrives fully flat, no instructions, but with a quick pull out, it’s pretty much set up. The seat is “stiff” going out and back in, but this gives the reassurance that it’ll stay set and not fold up on its own and weaken under you. I’ve included a video of our setting it up, taking it down - the one thing to note: the seat is VERY tight. We like this, but it can mean you need to ‘hold down’ the arms of the chair to keep the whole thing from coming off the ground, rather than just pulling up the seat. The seat is very comfortable. We can both see how sitting in this for hours would be possible. That said, I am a shorter man, and I do feel the cross pieces under the backs of my legs - I feel like it would grow weary after time time. To alleviate this I’ve tried various foot rests to get my legs up off these cross pieces and in doing so, it is again comfortable to me - not to mention having my feet up feels great. The seat itself is comfortable. The height it actually good. While my legs are shorter (I am 5’ 5”) a the same time I find that sitting in this chair is as comfortable as my wife finds it (5’ 7”). The material is Veronica and comfortable. There are strips of cloth mixed with leather on the arms, also making that comfortable and off the metal arms. text_fidelity_a:
Timex Full-Size Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor A good heart rate monitor and watch for people into fitness but are not super serious athletes. You can also wear this watch as a nice, functional regular watch too.

The operation of this watch is similar to the basic Timex ironman watches with some additional features (it's necessary to read the manual to understand all the features).

Pros: Watch is very comfortable - it's big but it stays in place. The strap is very adjustable and should fit nearly every wrist. The heart rate strap is also comfortable. The large face is a bonus because it's that much easier to glance down and see the numbers when you're running.
Lots of features - Chrono counts time and records your total workout length or laps, and gives an average HR for each lap. The interval timer counts down and can do timed intervals (eg. run for 8 min, walk 30 seconds). The review feature will give you average HR, max/min HR for the workout, how many minutes you spent in your "target" HR and calories burnt, which is nice to see if you want to judge how intense your workout was. It also gives the average HR for each of your laps.

It has an alarm clock and a really good Indiglo setting for the dark.

Very easy to use the HR monitor, basically put it on and press the HR button on the watch and it automatically starts getting HR data.

Cons: The review feature doesn't give the time spent in each HR zone over the whole workout, only your target HR zone. This seems like a big oversight because it's as important to see how much time you spend in the high HR "red" zones as well as the lower zones. This means that if you're running up and down varied terrain, you have to look down at your wrist to see what your HR is and remember what zone that is for you and guess how much time you've spent in each zone.

If you're only using one of the interval timers, you have to set the second interval timer to 0, which is very annoying. It would be easy to have a feature asking if you want to use one or two timers.

It doesn't store more than 1 workout review in the watch, so you have to write the info down if you want a record of your workouts. This is ridiculous for a watch at this price point.

It's not ANT+ compatible, so there's no way to increase the functionality like tying it to a GPS device. I suppose they want you to buy the next level up if you want to record that type of fitness data.
text_fidelity_b: Timex Full-Size Ironman Road Trainer Heart Rate Monitor

text_fidelity_a: Planet Bike Anatomic Relief System Classic Bike Seat- Men I ordered this bike because the saddle on my used Walmart (I admit it) road bike was killing my nether regions.  I have been riding for a year now and despite the origin of my bike, I have fallen in love with the sport and I usually go out for 15-20 mile rides and just enjoy the freedom it provides.  However, this season, my saddle became so painful that the fun was turning into sort of torture-endurance.  I decided to look for a new saddle but I hear so many stories of people spending all kinds of money trying to find the "right" saddle and if my bike is any indication, I don't have hundreds of dollars to spend to go through different saddles.  Anyway, I read the reviews on this saddle and being a bigger guy (240 lbs), I decided to give it a whirl based on the cheap cost.  Now, keep in mind that I also ordered a pair Pearl iZumi Men's Quest Cycling Shorts that I had read about on Amazon.  I say that because I figured a seat AND shorts might help.  On my first ride out with the saddle and the shorts, I was able to ride for 30 miles with hardly any pain!  I did notice that there would be a little pain when the bike short padding would get bunched up but after a readjustment, I was fine again.  It makes me wonder if the seat would have caused pain without the shorts.  I highly recommend buying shorts if you don't own any!  I wish I hadn't waited so long.  The padding makes a big difference.  I did notice the stickers coming off after the first ride but I don't really care about that.  I would rather have a plain seat then one with logos anyway.  I was surprised at how soft the seat was.  Some people have said that it is still a firm seat but after riding on my previous torture device, I feel that this is almost too padded.  I do feel that this is a great seat.  For the price, I figured I could give it a shot.  I'm definitely happy with the purchase!
text_fidelity_b: Planet Bike Anatomic Relief System Classic Bike Seat- Men

text_fidelity_a:
Wilson X Connected Smart Basketball with Sensor That Tracks Shots To be honest, I wouldn't have ordered this if it weren't a complementary Vine item, but I'm glad I did. I never even heard of such a ball, let along did I think it would work--it works!

A friend of mine is a basketball coach, so I dropped by with this ball. After getting curious looks of disbelief and questions as to if I missed the deadline on April fools, we started trying it out. The players really responded to it. It felt like a normal ball (a good one at that), but they could immediately track their stats. That's the real genius here. Most of us can seen when the ball goes in the net or not, but keeping track of shots made/missed in practice can be tedious. Plus you can hook some speakers (preferably bluetooth) up and have this make solo practice a game and keep tabs. It really works!

Wow, this sounds amazing! It sure does, but there are some limitations. For now iPhone (or iOS) only (works on iOS 9 btw). Android is coming. It also isn't for tracking layups or dunks, rather it's designed for 7+ foot shots. It's also not perfect. I was hoping for 95%+ accuracy, but 85-90% accuracy (requires a net to work at all btw). That's still amazing, but there's room for improvement. Also it's more useful in solo practice, as there are plenty of other ways to make group practice interesting. That's not to say it's not useful there, but $200 can probably be better used in that context.

As a solo practice tool, this is awesome. Like a fitbit or other modern doodad, this aids in accountability and adds a game like aspect to a mundane activity. Sure great players have always driven themselves to taking thousands of shots a day, but not everyone has that focus. This can definitely help, and while the accuracy is still a work in progress, over thousands of shots, it will show trends (and hopefully improvement). Plus it talks to social media, so if by chance you and a buddy have one, you can share stats and trash talk on Facebook. Isn't life grand! On a more serious note, it can show coach, dad (or mom), that you're using it and getting your reps in, to help justify that expensive summer basketball camp.

So is this a gadget for early adapters and hard core basketball players? Mostly. We all have different budgets, and for some $200 isn't much, but for many it is, and yeah, it's a niche. It'll do more to help your game than a pair of fancy shoes or expensive athletic wear, and for the gym rats who put in hours a day working on shooting, this is a great (and novel) addition to the arsenal. For everyone else, maybe wait a bit.

5 stars if you're in the niche
text_fidelity_b: Wilson X Connected Smart Basketball with Sensor That Tracks Shots

text_fidelity_a: HOMFUL Reclining High Back Low Beach Chair Compact Folding Protable Profile Low Seat for Adults with Padded Armrests,Cup Holder and Carry Bag for Outdoors Camping Lawn Hiking Travel Picnic [[VIDEOID:288708d09fce98e9909bb1f005690ad9]] We love to go to the beach during the summer and wanted a chair - rather than always laying on the ground. My wife also wanted something she could set by the waterline and have the water on her feet and legs. So these short, low chairs were on our watch list. When I had the chance, I grabbed this HOMFUL Camping Beach Chair and so far, we’re glad I did. The bag comes in a nice bag, making for easy carrying. I will say, getting the chair bag in the bag was a little tough - it would be nice if it had a little more room - but we did get it in with both of us working on it. The chair sets up and comes apart really very easily - one person can easily do it - with the back/top of the back of the chair coming off the lower section, then folding or unfolding. Note the video above. The chair is very low to the ground - we have had one other set that actually was not as low and it was low. Getting in and out is like it is on any such chair. The arms are slanted, so rolling in or out is actually kind of easier than pushing up. They are also coated with a sort of rubber like material, making them softer to lay your arms on them. Also, at a beach on a sunny day, making it more comfortable and less likely to burn your arm from the sun. The cup holder is decent - it lays under the side, and I think it’ll hold many options - we only tired a water bottle. Funny thing - I think there is a small pouch under the front - but once you’re in it, you can’t see it and I forgot about it - couldn’t even feel it. So forgot it was even there. The chair comes with a nice little blow up pillow and pouch for it - bet you can stick it in that front pouch if you find it. It was easy to blow up by mouth and when my wife was seated, I had her try it - it works, seems nice - but no way to attach to the chair - which would have been a nice addition. It’s mid-winter so no chance to try it out - yet - but from what we are experiencing here in the house, it’s going to be a nice addition to our days at the beach - and we can’t wait. We so far like this HOMFUL Camping Beach Chair and happy to have it.
text_fidelity_b: HOMFUL Reclining High Back Low Beach Chair Compact Folding Protable Profile Low Seat for Adults with Padded Armrests,Cup Holder and Carry Bag for Outdoors Camping Lawn Hiking Travel Picnic

text_fidelity_a:
Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks… I had high hopes for these electric socks. I mean, electric blankets have been around forever, right? So maybe, just maybe these would work. Sadly, they are utter crap.

When they arrived, they didn't look too bad. I was concerned about how much of the sock would have a heated area, but I figured, even a relatively small area might be helpful. I got some fresh AA batteries and loaded up the battery compartments. (There is a little pocket near the top outer side of each sock. There is a wire inside each of these that connects to the battery box.)

I felt just the faintest bit of warmth from one sock and nothing from the other. I put them on and honestly could not tell a difference between the non-working side and the one that was faintly warm. I thought perhaps they needed more time to warm up, so I continued wearing them hoping that would happen. I was busy working and after a couple of hours realized that they had never warmed up. So I decided to check the batteries, 'just in case,' they weren't fully charged. When I checked them on my battery tester, all four were completely dead even though I had gotten them from my fresh supply. I wondered if they could possibly have been bad to begin with, though that seemed highly unlikely. Then I wondered if the box had somehow drained the batteries.

Still holding out a tiny bit of hope the socks would warm, I got out more batteries. This time I checked them with my battery tester first, to make sure they were fully charged. They were. Again I felt the tiniest bit of warmth and thought, "Great! I guess the last batch of batteries were no good."

Put them on and again, could not feel the warmth. I later checked the fully charged batteries and .. you guessed it, they were drained. So not only did the stupid socks not work, they somehow drained EIGHT AA batteries!! What a waste of time and money. Needless to say, I want to send these back.

It's really a shame because a lot of people would love to have socks like this if they would actually work. I hope the manufacturer figures out a way to make them work AND do so without having to go through dozens of batteries each week.
text_fidelity_b: Electric Battery Operated Heated Socks Men Women Rechargeable Washable for Hunting Winter Skiing Mobile Warming Powered Battery Heated Socks…
